The DP World Tour has said they will deny LIV Golf players memberships if they take part in the league for 2027; Players need to be on the DP World Tour to be eligible for the Ryder Cup; Players must now 'make a choice'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

The DP World Tour will not allow any player who signs up to LIV Golf next season to be a member of its circuit in 2027.

Some of the world's top players were given conditional releases by the European tour in previous seasons, allowing them to compete on both circuits.

But DP World Tour chief executive officer Guy Kinnings has said players must now "make a choice".

In order to be eligible for Europe's Ryder Cup team, players must be members of the DP World Tour.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Kinnings told BBC Sport: "Players need to make a choice. We have rules and regulations which are there to protect our tour and which our members must all abide by.

"Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our tour."

LIV's future is in doubt after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew support at the end of the season and is going through Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in the United States.

The breakaway series has secured an initial funding commitment for a potential 300 million US dollars (£227m) investment from BC Partners Credit to help relaunch LIV 2.0 in 2027.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Deadlines for both tours fall next month and players will be asked to disclose which they intend to play on.

LIV players such as Jon Rahm, Tyrell Hatton and Victor Perez and Tom McKibbin are currently eligible to play on the DP World Tour under one of its membership categories.

Rahm is set to quit LIV Golf after refusing to accept new terms offered for its proposed relaunch and is reported to be owed up to 150m US dollars (£113m) for the remainder of the contract he signed almost three years ago.
